articles.headline: UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped
articles.description: A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.
articles.body:
A ban on football fans drinking in the stands during matches is outdated, discriminatory and should be scrapped, Andy Burnham said.

The Prime Minister said it was unfair for football fans to be singled out when supporters of other sports were able to drink while watching their teams.

The ban was put in place during the 1980s when concerns about hooliganism were at their height and covers the top-five tiers of English men's football.

But Everton fan Mr. Burnham said it was a measure from "an era when football was very different."

The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) welcomed the Prime Minister's words and said successful pilots of alcohol in the stands had been carried out in the women's game.

But police chiefs warned it would be "incredibly rash" to make changes without proper consultation with forces.

Mr. Burnham told reporters: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point.

"I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

"But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently from others."

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales in the top-five men's leagues.

FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said: "The FSA has always argued that it's unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match -- especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league.

"Many clubs are in favour as well. WSL and WSL2 ran a successful pilot, meaning fans can now drink in the stands at many grounds, while the EFL has long supported a trial.

"We welcome the Prime Minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed. We look forward to being part of that consultation."

A UK Football Policing Unit spokesman said police chiefs would welcome a meeting with Mr. Burnham to "explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans."

The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.

"It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games.

"Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.

articles.headline: McVay says Nacua's injury not 'long-term' concern, but Rams being cautious
articles.description: Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua does not have a hernia, but the team will "err on the side of caution" with the injury.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said he's not sure whether Puka Nacua will play in Week 3 but that the team is not worried that the wide receiver's injury will be "any sort of long-term threat."

Nacua did not play on Monday night with what was listed as a hip injury on the injury report, but McVay later clarified that Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin.

McVay said Nacua does not have a hernia, but the team is being cautious with the injury.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just ... it's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said. "And so you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

The Rams did not practice on Wednesday, instead holding a walkthrough on the short week, but the team estimated that Nacua would not have taken part if they had. McVay said the team will see whether Nacua will practice on Thursday, adding that he knows Nacua is "frustrated" with the situation.

"We all want him to be able to be out there, but we want him to be able to return to performance, not just be able to just kind of gut through it," McVay said.

Last week, McVay said Nacua's injury wasn't related to the psoas injury that caused him to miss time in August. In the Rams' season opener, Nacua led Los Angeles with five catches for 74 yards on nine targets.

The Rams play the Denver Broncos in Week 3 on Sunday Night Football.

articles.headline: Judge says he intends to be available for AL Wild Card Series
articles.description: Yankees' slugger Aaron Judge told ESPN on Wednesday that he intends to be ready for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium next Tuesday.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- New York Yankees star Aaron Judge is not giving up on being available for the start of the postseason.

The three-time MVP told ESPN on Wednesday that he intends to be ready for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium next Tuesday.

"That's what the plan is," Judge said. "Try to get my body ready so I'm ready to go."

Judge was placed on the injured list Saturday with a right calf strain, ending his regular season. He later specified that the strain is in the soleus muscle, which he noted is essential for running and hitting. He confirmed that he received a PPP injection Monday and was waiting for clearance to resume activity that involved the leg.

On Tuesday, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said he does not expect to have Judge available for the Wild Card series, though he did not rule out the possibility.

"We're planning on him not being a part of that," Boone said.

Judge, 34, said he's had discussions with decision-makers in the organization about his prognosis, which has not been made clear publicly.

"We've done a lot of talks, but I can't control what people say," Judge said. "So you'll have to talk to them about that."

Asked if he expects to be on the roster, Judge said he didn't know.

"I don't make the roster," Judge said. "I've got no idea."

Judge said he suffered the injury during the Yankees' 5-4 loss to the Minnesota Twins on Sept. 16, in his seventh game back after missing more than three months with a fractured rib. He and the club were initially hopeful that it was minor, but he underwent an MRI on Thursday that revealed the strain.

Judge went 4-for-23 with 13 strikeouts, one walk, and one home run in 24 plate appearances after returning from his fractured rib without a rehab assignment. Overall, he batted .241 with 18 home runs and an .871 OPS in 66 games, which include playing with the fractured rib for over a month until late May.

The Yankees went 41-25 and averaged 5.12 runs per game with Judge in the lineup this season. Entering Wednesday, they're 49-42 and averaging 4.15 runs per game without him. They will likely face the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series for the second consecutive postseason after knocking out their rivals in three games with Judge in their lineup last October.

"We've got games to win," Judge said. "I'm getting paid to play games for the New York Yankees so I'll get back as soon as I can."

articles.headline: Commanders say clip didn't reflect team response to Daniels injury
articles.description: After a short video clip showed a number of Commanders walking past Jayden Daniels as he was being helped by medical personnel Sunday, many players fired back at the takes being spouted on social media, emphasizing, "It's bulls--- what people are saying."
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders players rejected the notion that they didn't care about Jayden Daniels as he was being tended to by athletic trainers after dislocating his left elbow Sunday.

A short video clip from the Fox broadcast showed a number of Commanders players walking past Daniels as he was being helped by medical personnel.

It led to multiple posts on social media, as well as analysts weighing in, comparing the scene to New York Giants players gathering around quarterback Jaxson Dart after he injured his knee Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams. 

"It's bulls--- what people are saying," Washington left tackle Brandon Coleman said. "Jay's our guy and he's been our guy. There's no malice behind it."

Daniels' injury happened on the last play of the first half, which led to confusion by the players about what they could do or how long they could linger.

Though the camera showed them walking past Daniels, almost all waited on the sideline and watched from there. A number of them then returned to Daniels' side after trainers had popped his dislocated elbow back into place.

But Washington coach Dan Quinn said, "When the half is over, the referees are saying, 'Man, I can't delay the half. They can't stay on the field.' The players were like, 'No, we want to stay.'

"So it's just the opposite of that. They were gutted. They love this guy. So halftime was hard and emotional in that space."

An NFL halftime lasts 13 minutes. One player said Quinn told the players to return to the locker room. Another player, who remained on the sideline, said an official told him they had only eight more minutes remaining so they'd better head inside.

Daniels had his foot stepped on while pulling away from under center, causing him to lose his balance. He tried to steady himself with his left arm as he fell backward, causing it to dislocate. After the play, he stayed on the ground as some players gathered around him.

Center Nick Allegretti said after the game that he had called for trainers. Daniels then started to run off, with his left arm clutched to his side. He then went back to the ground as some players paused, saw the trainers coming out to the field and continued walking.

"We stayed on the field and once they got it situated and did what they had to do we checked on him," Coleman said. "Dan told most [players] to go into the locker room. But it's tough to go in when you see something like that. You see the whole starting line out there, a bunch of receivers, some defensive guys."

A number of players indeed were seen standing around Daniels -- as Coleman said there were offensive linemen, defensive linemen, defensive backs, receivers and running backs. Linebackers were seen exiting as well as Daniels' cart drove away. Coleman and fellow lineman Josh Conerly Jr., were among the last two to leave, along with Quinn and backup quarterbacks Marcus Mariota and Athan Kaliakmanis.

articles.headline: Seahawks' Darnold 'on a good track' to play vs. Commanders
articles.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is "on a good track" to play Sunday against the Commanders, coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのダーノルド、コマンダーズ戦出場に向けて「順調な経過」
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのクォーターバック、サム・ダーノルドは日曜日のコマンダーズ戦出場に向けて「順調な経過をたどっている」とマイク・マクドナルドHCが水曜日に語った。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday that quarterback Sam Darnold is "on a good track" to play Sunday against the Washington Commanders after missing most of the first two games with a glute injury.

Darnold is practicing Wednesday for the first time since he was hurt early in the season opener. Macdonald said he won't take every practice rep initially, and that his workload will be ramped up as the week progresses.

Does Darnold have to be fully healthy to start?

"I don't know what fully healthy means," Macdonald said. "I think we'll make a decision at some point before Friday's over. I don't think we'd go into the weekend not knowing if he's going to play. But it's on a good track right now, assuming today goes well."

Backup Drew Lock has quarterbacked the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks to a 2-0 record. Since Darnold went down on the fifth play of their 13-10 win over the New England Patriots in Week 1, Lock has completed nearly 73% of his passes with four touchdowns and zero turnovers. His Total QBR of 88.8 in the team's 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday was the third-best mark of his career.

Through two games, Lock ranks fourth among all quarterbacks in Total QBR at 85.8.

Macdonald was asked whether Lock's play allows the Seahawks to be more conservative with Darnold's return.

"If it was something where he was at risk of getting worse over the normal risk you take by taking the field, that might be part of the conversation," Macdonald said. "But really it's a function at this point of does he feel good enough to play."

Macdonald said safety Nick Emmanwori will have a "significantly higher" workload this week after playing nine snaps in his season debut in Week 2. Emmanwori missed the opener following July ankle surgery and was listed as having a hip injury last week.

"We'll see how the game unfolds, see how he feels," Macdonald said, "but he'll be out there a good bit."

Seattle placed right guard Anthony Bradford (knee/hip) on injured reserve Wednesday. Macdonald said he won't be sidelined long term. In a corresponding move, the Seahawks signed safety Rodney Thomas II off their practice squad. He started the first two games while Ty Okada (hamstring) was out.

articles.headline: How Chiefs TE Travis Kelce turned wedding shape into football shape
articles.description: Kelce, who leads the NFL in YAC, has had an average route speed of 11.56 mph, the fastest he's been since 2022.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- At some point late Sunday night, perhaps after he bearhugged kicker Harrison Butker, who made the game-winning field goal in the Kansas City Chiefs' overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts, star tight end Travis Kelce learned he earned yet another NFL record in his illustrious career.

In the second quarter, Kelce caught a short pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes, a reception he turned into an 11-yard gain. That moment was when Kelce broke the record for the most yards after the catch in NFL history, passing Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk.

"I had no idea," Kelce said after the game of breaking the record. "It's pretty freaking cool, man, to be in talks with guys like Marshall Faulk, Larry Fitzgerald, Terrell Owens. That's some pretty cool stuff, man. Those are the guys I grew up watching. Guys like that fueled my love for this game."

Not only has Kelce, 36, recorded 6,287 yards after the catch in his 14-year career, but he also leads the league in the statistic this season (128), which represents the most such yardage in his first two games of a season in his career, according to ESPN Research.

Such impressive production has helped the Chiefs start with a 2-0 record and provided evidence that Kelce's individual performance has been better than the past two seasons, when he showed dips in speed and athleticism.

"Travis worked his tail off," coach Andy Reid said Monday. "He likes his surrounding cast, too, which sure helps as just an extra challenge there to make sure that you're up there and competing and doing your part.

"I know everybody questioned the wedding and all that. Would he be out of shape and honeymooning the whole time? But he works his rear end off. [With] Taylor [Swift], you're putting on four-hour shows. You've got to work hard, too. I'm sure she kicks him in the butt a little bit there, too."

Kelce entered training camp in late July just three weeks after his wedding to Swift, the international pop star. His transition from wedding shape into football shape was smooth, too, since he didn't miss a single practice and was still one of the Chiefs' best pass catchers, especially in one-on-one drills against linebackers and safeties.

Kelce's average route speed this season, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, is 11.56 miles per hour, the fastest he's been since 2022.

"It's not as much about the shape that I look like I'm in," Kelce said, smiling. "It's about the grit that I have and the heart that I have to get that ball north."

One of the best examples against the Colts was Kelce's highlight inside the red zone. In the first quarter, Kelce showcased his speed and quickness to run away from nickel cornerback Justin Walley for a 13-yard touchdown.

"I saw Cover 4 and that the flat defender was a little inside of me," said Kelce, who finished with a game-high 101 receiving yards. "I knew Pat was going to give me a chance, so just get the ball north and find a way to get into the end zone."

articles.headline: 49ers place starting DT C.J. West on IR due to knee injury
articles.description: 49ers defensive tackle C.J. West, who is going to miss at least a chunk of the season with a bone chip in his knee that will require surgery, was placed on injured reserve Wednesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Add defensive tackle to the list of positions where the San Francisco 49ers are growing thin after the team placed starting nose tackle C.J. West on injured reserve Wednesday.

On the heels of a season-ending patellar injury to Alfred Collins and a high ankle sprain for rookie James Thompson Jr., West is going to miss at least a chunk of the season with a bone chip in his knee that will require surgery.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said West's injury is not season-ending, but it is another blow to a position that has just two healthy players remaining from the five that originally made the 53-man roster.

The Niners didn't initially list West among their injuries coming out of their Week 2 win against the Miami Dolphins, but Shanahan said West's knee has been battling "something" since training camp.

"I don't know if this is the same or if it was something new," Shanahan said. "But it was bothering him a lot after the game."

There's no timeline for West's return, but the 49ers added more depth at defensive tackle on Wednesday. San Francisco signed veteran Naquan Jones, who has played in 60 games with eight starts for the Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans, off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.

Jones, who projects as more of a nose tackle and a direct replacement for West, took part in his first practice with the Niners on Wednesday afternoon. As it stands, the Niners have just three healthy defensive tackles -- Osa Odighizuwa, Gracen Halton and Jones -- on the roster.

San Francisco also has three more defensive tackles on the practice squad in Kevin Givens, Sebastian Valdez and McKinnley Jackson. Defensive end Keion White also can move inside to tackle in obvious passing situations.

For now, Shanahan said the Niners will evaluate those practice squad options to see who else can help fill in for West.

"Anytime you have five D tackles make a team and you're down to two of them after two games, that's always a concern for anybody," Shanahan said. "We were able to sign one new guy and then we got three guys on practice squad that will be competing to see who's up. We got guys there in this building, so we got to see how those guys step it up."

As for another injury-ravaged position, the Niners signed veteran receiver Brandin Cooks to the practice squad Wednesday. Cooks' arrival coincides with a high ankle sprain for Demarcus Robinson as well as a sore hip for Mike Evans that left the Niners without either participating in Wednesday's practice.

Robinson will miss three to six weeks and could land on injured reserve while the Niners plan to manage Evans this week with hopes he will play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. San Francisco is also without Ricky Pearsall (knee, out for the season) and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, currently on IR).

articles.headline: Braves activate set-up man Suarez, target 2 appearances ahead of playoffs
articles.description: Braves reliever Robert Suarez, who has been sidelined more than three months with right elbow inflammation, was activated with the aim of being used Wednesday night and again Saturday ahead of the postseason.
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- The Braves activated relief pitcher Robert Suarez on Wednesday after he spent more than three months on the injured list with right elbow inflammation.

Braves manager Walt Weiss said he will aim to use Suarez on Wednesday night against Cincinnati and again Saturday against Miami to prepare him for the postseason. If things go according to plan, Suarez will resume his role as the Braves' set-up man for closer Raisel Iglesias.

Suarez thrived in his first year with the Braves before to the injury, posting an 0.56 ERA in 31 appearances out of the bullpen. The two-time All-Star has pitched in three postseasons with San Diego before coming to Atlanta with a 2.45 ERA in 12 games.

Suarez pitched a scoreless inning Sunday for Triple-A Gwinnett in his only rehab appearance.

The Braves sent right-hander Owen Murphy to Triple-A Gwinnett to make room on the roster for Suarez.
